statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Alcoholic Liquor or Drug
offense_class: Class W Misdemeanor (first/second); Class W Felony (third); Class IIA Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated or had actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcoholic liquor or any drug
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher within two hours of driving
On any highway or anywhere throughout the state
enhancements: Refusal of chemical test (enhanced license revocation)
Third offense within 15 years (Class W Felony)
notes: Nebraska uses a 15-year lookback period for prior offenses. Implied consent under § 60-6,197. Ignition interlock required for most offenses. Administrative license revocation is separate from criminal penalties.

offense_class: Class W Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated or had actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impaired ability to operate
No prior DUI convictions within 15 years
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (aggravated first offense — enhanced penalties)
notes: Court may impose 6 months probation in lieu of 7-day mandatory minimum. Ignition interlock device may be required. BAC .15+ is an aggravated first offense with longer revocation.

offense_class: Class W Misdemeanor (second); Class W Felony (third); Class IIA Felony (fourth+)
elements: Defendant operated or had actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impaired ability to operate
One or more prior DUI convictions within 15 years
mandatory_minimum: 30 days (second); 90 days (third, cannot be suspended); 2 years (fourth+, cannot be suspended)
notes: Second offense: 18-month license revocation. Third: 15-year revocation. Fourth+: 15-year revocation. Ignition interlock required for all repeat offenders. Mandatory substance abuse evaluation.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated or had actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any drug
To a degree that rendered the defendant incapable of safely driving
Or while under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limits in Nebraska. Prosecution must prove actual impairment. Blood or urine testing may be used. Includes prescription medications that impair driving.

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor (first); Class II Misdemeanor (second); Class I Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
In such a manner as to indicate an indifferent or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Willful reckless driving under § 60-6,214 carries enhanced penalties. License revocation may be imposed.

statute_title: Accidents — Duty to Stop — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class IIIA Felony (injury/death); Class II Misdemeanor (property damage under § 60-696)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide name, address, and registration information
notes: Leaving the scene involving injury or death is a Class IIIA Felony. Property damage only is a Class II Misdemeanor. Must also render reasonable assistance to injured persons.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (negligence); Class IIA Felony (DUI involved); Class IIIA Felony (reckless operation)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a manner constituting negligence, reckless operation, or while DUI
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: Nebraska has three levels of motor vehicle homicide based on culpability. DUI-related vehicular homicide carries the most severe penalties.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a criminally negligent manner
Proximately causing the death of another person
Not involving DUI or reckless operation
notes: Lowest level of motor vehicle homicide. Requires proof of criminal negligence — more than ordinary negligence but less than recklessness.

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor (first); Class II Misdemeanor (second); Class I Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While defendant's operator's license was suspended, revoked, or impounded
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Additional 1-year extension of revocation period. Driving during a DUI-related revocation may result in additional criminal charges.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (basic); Class IV Felony (willful reckless driving during flight)
elements: A peace officer attempted to make a lawful stop
Defendant willfully fled to avoid arrest or citation
Officer was in uniform or operating a marked vehicle
enhancements: Willful reckless driving during flight (Class IV Felony under § 28-905(1)(b))
Resulting in serious bodily injury or death
notes: Basic flight is a Class I Misdemeanor. If defendant drives recklessly during the flight, it becomes a Class IV Felony. Death resulting may be charged as motor vehicle homicide.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (most substances); Infraction/Misdemeanor (marijuana, small amounts)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed on Nebraska controlled substance schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school, playground, or youth center (enhanced penalty)
notes: Nebraska classifies most controlled substance possession as a Class IV Felony. Marijuana has separate, lesser provisions. Drug court diversion may be available.

offense_class: Infraction (≤1 oz, first); Class IV Misdemeanor (≤1 oz, second); Class IIIA Misdemeanor (≤1 oz, third); Class IIIA Misdemeanor (1 oz–1 lb)
penalty_max: Citation only (≤1 oz first); 5 days (≤1 oz second); 7 days (≤1 oz third); 7 days (1 oz–1 lb first)
fine_max: $300 (≤1 oz first); $500 (≤1 oz second); $500 (≤1 oz third); $500 (1 oz–1 lb first)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
Without lawful authority
notes: Nebraska partially decriminalized small amounts of marijuana. First offense under 1 ounce is an infraction (no jail). Over 1 pound is a felony. Nebraska does not have legal recreational marijuana.

offense_class: Class IV Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in Nebraska
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or youth facility
notes: No minimum quantity for possession charge. Larger quantities may support distribution or trafficking charges.

offense_class: Class IV Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
enhancements: Possession near a school or youth facility
notes: Methamphetamine is a high-priority enforcement target in Nebraska. Drug courts and treatment-based diversion are available in many jurisdictions.

statute_title: Distribution, Delivery, or Manufacturing of a Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class II Felony (most substances); Class IIA Felony (marijuana ≤1 lb)
elements: Defendant manufactured, distributed, delivered, or dispensed a controlled substance
Or possessed with intent to distribute or deliver
The substance was a controlled substance under Nebraska law
mandatory_minimum: 1 year (general); 3 years (to a minor or near school under § 28-416(2))
enhancements: Distribution to a minor (3-year mandatory minimum)
Distribution near a school, playground, or youth center (§ 28-416(2))
notes: Nebraska's trafficking penalties are among the nation's most severe. Distribution near schools or to minors carries a mandatory 3-year minimum. Exceptionally large quantities may trigger federal prosecution.

statute_title: Distribution or Delivery of Controlled Substance
offense_class: Class II Felony (Schedule I/II); Class IIA Felony (Schedule III); Class IIIA Felony (Schedule IV/V)
penalty_max: 50 years (Schedule I/II); 20 years (Schedule III); 5 years (Schedule IV/V)
elements: Defendant distributed, delivered, or dispensed a controlled substance
To another person
Knowingly or intentionally
enhancements: Distribution near a school or youth facility
notes: Penalty depends on the schedule of the controlled substance. Schedule I and II substances carry the most severe penalties.

offense_class: Class II Felony (most substances); Class III Felony (marijuana cultivation)
elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
Including cultivating, producing, preparing, or compounding
Without lawful authority
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries the most severe penalties. Environmental cleanup liability may be imposed. Child endangerment charges may also apply.

offense_class: Infraction (first); Class IV Misdemeanor (second); Class IIIA Misdemeanor (third+)
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use the paraphernalia to introduce a controlled substance into the body
Items as defined in § 28-439
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Class I Misdemeanor under § 28-442)
notes: First offense is an infraction with a fine only. Distribution of paraphernalia to a minor is a more serious offense.

offense_class: Class II Felony (Schedule I/II); Class IIA Felony (Schedule III); Class IIIA Felony (Schedule IV/V)
penalty_max: 50 years (Schedule I/II); 20 years (Schedule III); 5 years (Schedule IV/V)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture, distribute, or deliver
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other evidence
enhancements: Proximity to schools or youth facilities
notes: Intent to distribute is inferred from circumstances including quantity, packaging, presence of scales, large amounts of cash, and communications.

offense_class: Class IA Felony
elements: Defendant purposely and with deliberate and premeditated malice killed another person
Or killed another person in the perpetration of or attempt to perpetrate certain felonies (felony murder)
enhancements: Aggravating circumstances for death penalty consideration
Victim was a law enforcement officer
notes: Nebraska has the death penalty but rarely imposes it. Lethal injection is the method. Life imprisonment means life without parole. Felony murder applies to killings during robbery, sexual assault, arson, kidnapping, and hijacking.

offense_class: Class IB Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of a person intentionally
But without premeditation
notes: Second-degree murder requires intentional killing without the deliberation and premeditation required for first-degree murder.

offense_class: Class IIA Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally killed another person
Under a sudden quarrel or in the heat of passion
Caused by legally adequate provocation
notes: Nebraska's manslaughter statute covers what other states call voluntary manslaughter. The provocation must be of a nature that would provoke a reasonable person.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (negligent); Class IV Felony (reckless)
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
Through criminal negligence or recklessness
Without lawful justification
notes: Nebraska does not have a standalone involuntary manslaughter statute. Non-vehicular negligent killings may be charged under manslaughter. Vehicular deaths are charged under motor vehicle homicide.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused serious bodily injury to another person
enhancements: Use of a deadly or dangerous weapon (§ 28-309)
Against a peace officer, health care provider, or other protected person
notes: First-degree assault is the most serious non-homicide offense against persons. Serious bodily injury means injury creating a substantial risk of death or causing permanent disfigurement.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor; Class IIIA Felony (third+ within 12 years)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
Or threatened another in a menacing manner
enhancements: Third offense within 12 years (Class IIIA Felony)
Against a protected person (officer, healthcare worker)
notes: Third-degree assault is Nebraska's basic assault offense. Threatening behavior without actual injury is also covered. Repeat offenses within 12 years become felonies.

statute_title: Assault in the Third Degree (Battery Equivalent)
offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
Through physical contact
notes: Nebraska does not have a separate battery statute. Offensive physical contact resulting in injury is prosecuted as third-degree assault.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant took property from the person or presence of another
By force, threat of force, or intimidation
With the intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: All robbery in Nebraska is a Class II Felony. The distinction between robbery grades is based on weapon use and injury, but the felony class remains the same.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant took property from the person or presence of another
By force, threat of force, or intimidation
While armed with a deadly weapon
enhancements: Use of a firearm (mandatory minimum enhancement under § 28-1205)
notes: Nebraska does not have a separate armed robbery statute. Use of a deadly weapon during robbery triggers the mandatory firearm enhancement under § 28-1205.

offense_class: Class IA Felony (not voluntarily released); Class II Felony (voluntarily released unharmed)
elements: Defendant abducted another person without consent
With intent to hold for ransom, as a shield or hostage
Or to facilitate commission of a felony
Or to terrorize the victim or a third person
enhancements: Victim not voluntarily released alive and unharmed (Class IA Felony — life)
notes: Class IA Felony (life imprisonment) if victim is not voluntarily released alive and unharmed in a safe place. Voluntary release before prosecution reduces to Class II Felony.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally started a fire or caused an explosion
Placing another person in danger of death or serious bodily harm
Or damaging or destroying a building or occupied structure
enhancements: Person inside the structure at the time
notes: First-degree arson requires danger to human life. Second-degree arson (§ 28-503) covers intentional damage to buildings without human endangerment (Class III Felony). Third-degree arson (§ 28-504) covers other property (Class IV Felony).

statute_title: Attempted Murder in the First Degree
offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step
Toward the commission of first-degree murder
With the intent to kill another person
notes: Attempt to commit a Class IA or IB Felony is a Class II Felony under § 28-201. Attempted murder carries up to 50 years imprisonment.

offense_class: Class IIA Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused bodily injury to another
With a dangerous instrument
enhancements: Against a peace officer or protected person
notes: Second-degree assault covers assaults with dangerous instruments. A dangerous instrument is any item that can cause death or serious bodily injury in the manner it is used.

offense_class: Class II Misdemeanor (<$500); Class I Misdemeanor ($500–$1,500); Class IV Felony ($1,500–$5,000); Class IIA Felony (>$5,000)
elements: Defendant took or exercised control over movable property of another
With the intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: Nebraska grades theft by value. Multiple thefts may be aggregated to reach felony thresholds under § 28-518.

offense_class: Class IV Felony ($1,500–$5,000); Class IIA Felony (>$5,000)
elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in § 28-511 through § 28-515
Value of property was $1,500 or more
notes: Nebraska does not use the term 'grand theft.' Felony theft begins at $1,500. Values may be aggregated from a common scheme.

offense_class: Class II Misdemeanor (<$500); Class I Misdemeanor ($500–$1,500)
elements: Defendant committed theft as defined in § 28-511 through § 28-515
Value of property was less than $1,500
notes: Nebraska does not use the term 'petty theft.' Misdemeanor theft applies when value is under $1,500.

offense_class: Same grading as general theft by value
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant concealed merchandise of any store or retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise
Without paying the purchase price
notes: Shoplifting is a specific form of theft under Nebraska law. Civil recovery by merchants is also available. Penalty grading follows general theft value thresholds.

offense_class: Class IIA Felony (occupied dwelling); Class III Felony (unoccupied building)
elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and forcibly broke and entered
Any real estate or any improvement erected thereon
With intent to commit a felony, steal property, or commit any offense
notes: Nebraska distinguishes between burglary of a dwelling and other buildings. Burglary of an occupied dwelling is the most serious form.

offense_class: Class IIA Felony
elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and forcibly broke and entered
A dwelling house or any structure appurtenant to a dwelling
With intent to commit a felony, steal, or commit any offense
notes: Burglary of a dwelling is a Class IIA Felony regardless of whether anyone was home at the time.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (most vehicles); Class IIA Felony (high value)
elements: Defendant took or exercised control over a motor vehicle of another
With intent to deprive the owner of the vehicle
notes: Motor vehicle theft is graded by vehicle value under general theft thresholds. Most vehicle thefts exceed the $1,500 felony threshold.

offense_class: Graded same as theft by value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value of property
fine_max: Same as theft by value of property
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing the property was stolen or believing it was probably stolen
With the intent to deprive the owner
notes: Graded as theft by value of the stolen property. Belief that property is probably stolen is sufficient — absolute knowledge not required.

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor (<$500); Class I Misdemeanor ($500–$1,500); Class IV Felony ($1,500–$5,000); Class III Felony (>$5,000)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged property of another
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Damage to public property or utilities
notes: Nebraska uses 'criminal mischief' for vandalism. Graded by the amount of damage. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or secretly remained in a building or occupied structure
Knowing that entry or remaining was not licensed or privileged
notes: First-degree trespass applies to buildings and occupied structures. Second-degree trespass (§ 28-521) applies to fenced or posted property (Class III Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor to Class III Felony (graded by damage amount)
penalty_max: Varies by damage amount (see vandalism entry)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged property of another
Or intentionally tampered with property so as to endanger persons or property
notes: Same statute as vandalism. Criminal mischief includes tampering with utilities, transportation, and communication systems.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first/second); Class IIIA Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant intentionally and knowingly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
Or threatened a family or household member in a menacing manner
Family or household member includes spouse, former spouse, person residing together, person with shared child
enhancements: Third offense within 12 years (Class IIIA Felony)
Use of a dangerous instrument (§ 28-323(2) — second degree, Class IIA Felony)
Serious bodily injury (§ 28-323(1) — first degree, Class II Felony)
notes: Nebraska has three degrees of domestic assault. First degree (serious bodily injury) is a Class II Felony. Second degree (with dangerous instrument) is Class IIA Felony. Third degree is Class I Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally and knowingly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
First or second offense
enhancements: Use of a dangerous instrument (elevated to second degree)
Serious bodily injury (elevated to first degree)
notes: Court typically orders batterers' intervention program. Victims eligible for protection orders under § 42-924.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (negligent/no injury); Class IIIA Felony (injury); Class IIA Felony (serious injury); Class IB Felony (death)
penalty_max: 1 year (no injury); 5 years (injury); 20 years (serious injury); Life (death)
elements: Defendant, being a parent, guardian, or person having custody of a child
Knowingly, intentionally, or negligently caused or permitted the child to be
Placed in a situation that endangered the child's life or health
enhancements: Death (Class IB Felony — 20 years to life)
notes: Nebraska's child abuse statute covers a wide range of conduct from negligent treatment to intentional acts causing death. Grading depends on resulting harm.

offense_class: Class IIIA Felony (injury); Class IIA Felony (serious injury); Class IB Felony (death)
elements: Defendant knowingly, intentionally, or negligently caused or permitted
A minor child to be cruelly confined, punished, neglected, or deprived of necessary care
Resulting in bodily injury
notes: Child abuse resulting in death carries 20 years to life. DHHS involvement typically accompanies criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first); Class IV Felony (second+)
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant knowingly violated a provision of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation (Class IV Felony)
notes: Second or subsequent violation within 12 years is a Class IV Felony. Law enforcement must arrest upon probable cause of violation.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first); Class IV Felony (second+ or with credible threat)
elements: Defendant willfully harassed another person or a family or household member of such person
With the intent to intimidate, threaten, or frighten
On two or more separate occasions
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class IV Felony)
Credible threat of death or bodily injury
Violation of a protective order while stalking
notes: Stalking includes following, monitoring, surveillance, threatening, and communicating to the victim or about the victim. Includes cyberstalking.

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor (first); Class I Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Communicated a threat to injure the person, property, or reputation of the threatened person
Or engaged in a course of alarming conduct directed at the victim
notes: Harassment includes telephone harassment, electronic communication harassment, and in-person threatening conduct.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class IIIA Felony (abuse/neglect); Class IIA Felony (serious injury); Class IB Felony (death)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult
Vulnerable adult includes persons 65+ or persons with disabilities
Defendant was a caretaker or person responsible for the adult's care
notes: Nebraska Adult Protective Services investigates. Financial exploitation of vulnerable adults is separately addressed under § 28-386. Mandatory reporting for suspected abuse.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first); Class IV Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant carried a weapon concealed on or about their person
Including a revolver, pistol, bowie knife, dirk, or other dangerous weapon
Without a valid concealed handgun permit
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class IV Felony)
notes: Nebraska adopted constitutional carry (permitless concealed carry) effective September 2023. Some location restrictions remain. Concealed Handgun Permit still available for reciprocity.

statute_title: Possession of a Deadly Weapon by a Prohibited Person
offense_class: Class ID Felony
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm, knife, or other deadly weapon
Defendant was a prohibited person (convicted felon, fugitive, under 18, or other prohibited category)
Possession was knowing
enhancements: Possession of a firearm (vs. other deadly weapon)
Commission of another felony while in possession
notes: One of the most seriously graded weapons offenses in Nebraska. Mandatory minimum of 3 years. Prohibited persons include felons, fugitives, persons under indictment for a felony, and persons subject to domestic violence protection orders.

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor (first); Class I Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed handgun
In a location where carrying is prohibited by law
Such as a school, courthouse, polling place, or private property with posted notice
notes: Even under constitutional carry, certain locations remain prohibited. Private property owners may prohibit concealed carry with posted notice.

statute_title: Discharge of Firearm at an Inhabited Building or Vehicle
offense_class: Class IC Felony (at dwelling); Class ID Felony (at vehicle or other building)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly discharged a firearm
At an inhabited dwelling house, building, or occupied vehicle
notes: Very severe penalties with mandatory minimums. Discharge at an inhabited dwelling is a Class IC Felony with a 5-year mandatory minimum.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (general); Class IIA Felony (≥$5,000 or multiple victims)
elements: Defendant knowingly used, possessed, or transferred any personal identifying information of another
With intent to commit any unlawful act
Including obtaining credit, goods, services, or anything of value
enhancements: Victim is a minor or elderly person
notes: Identity theft involving $5,000+ or 3+ victims is a Class IIA Felony. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Graded same as theft by value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value (up to 20 years for >$5,000)
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant exercised unauthorized control over the property
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Nebraska prosecutes embezzlement under the general theft statute. The fiduciary or employment relationship is the distinguishing element.

offense_class: Class III Felony
elements: Defendant falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
With intent to deceive or harm
The instrument purported to be money, securities, stamps, or government documents
notes: First-degree forgery covers currency, securities, and government documents. Second-degree forgery (§ 28-603) covers other documents like checks and contracts (Class IV Felony).

offense_class: Class III Felony
elements: Defendant falsely made or possessed counterfeit currency, securities, or stamps
With intent to deceive or defraud
notes: Counterfeiting of federal currency typically prosecuted federally. Nebraska's first-degree forgery covers state-level counterfeiting offenses.

offense_class: Class II Misdemeanor (<$500); Class I Misdemeanor ($500–$1,500); Class IV Felony ($1,500–$5,000); Class III Felony (>$5,000)
elements: Defendant issued or passed a check or similar instrument
Knowing the check would not be paid by the drawee
Or issued a check drawn on an account with insufficient funds
notes: Failure to make good within 10 days of notice creates a presumption of knowledge. Graded by the face value of the check.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (<$5,000); Class III Felony ($5,000–$25,000); Class IIA Felony (>$25,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly and with intent to defraud
Presented or caused to be presented a false claim for insurance benefits
Or concealed information material to a claim
notes: Nebraska grades insurance fraud by the value of the fraudulent claim. Includes auto, health, property, and all other insurance types.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Forged Instrument — Credit Card
offense_class: Class IV Felony
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or account number of another
Without the cardholder's authorization
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
With intent to defraud
notes: Nebraska prosecutes credit card fraud under forgery, theft by deception, or identity theft statutes depending on circumstances.

offense_class: Class IIA Felony
fine_max: $25,000 or twice the value of property involved
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved was derived from criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source of funds
notes: Nebraska's money laundering statute covers proceeds from any criminal activity. Fine may be up to twice the value of the property involved.

offense_class: Graded same as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
By creating or reinforcing a false impression
Including false impressions of law, value, intention, or other state of mind
notes: Nebraska's general fraud offense is theft by deception. Graded by value of property obtained.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual penetration
Without consent of the victim
By force, threat of force, or coercion
Or when the victim was physically or mentally incapable of resisting or appraising the nature of the conduct
enhancements: Victim was 12 years of age or younger (§ 28-319.01 — 15 years to life)
notes: First-degree sexual assault is the most serious sexual offense. Second degree (§ 28-320) covers sexual contact without consent (Class III Felony). Third degree covers other circumstances.

offense_class: Class II Felony
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual penetration
Without consent of the victim
By force, threat of force, or coercion
notes: Nebraska does not use the term 'rape' in its statutes. What other states call rape is prosecuted as first-degree sexual assault.

offense_class: Class II Misdemeanor (first); Class I Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant exposed genitals to another person
With the intent to affront or alarm
In a public place or place accessible to the public
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class I Misdemeanor)
notes: Repeated offenses carry increased penalties. May require sex offender registration depending on circumstances.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first); Class IV Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant performed or offered or agreed to perform sexual acts
In return for money or other thing of value
Or defendant solicited another to perform sexual acts for compensation
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class IV Felony)
Solicitation of a minor (trafficking charges under § 28-831)
notes: Both the person soliciting and the person offering are subject to prosecution. Solicitation involving a minor triggers human trafficking charges.

statute_title: Visual Depiction of Sexually Explicit Conduct — Child
offense_class: Class IC Felony (production); Class ID Felony (distribution); Class IIA Felony (possession)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, manufactured, or distributed visual depictions
Of sexually explicit conduct involving a child
Defendant knew or should have known the subject was a child
enhancements: Prior conviction for sexual offense involving a child
notes: Production and distribution carry mandatory minimum sentences. Each image/video may constitute a separate count.

statute_title: Failure to Comply with Sex Offender Registration Act
offense_class: Class IV Felony (first); Class IIIA Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register, update, or verify registration
Or defendant provided false information
enhancements: Second or subsequent failure to register
notes: Nebraska's Sex Offender Registration Act requires registration for 15 years, 25 years, or lifetime depending on the offense. Quarterly verification required.

statute_title: Sexual Assault of a Child — First Degree
offense_class: Class IB Felony
elements: Defendant subjected a person under 12 years of age to sexual penetration
Or defendant was 19 years of age or older and subjected a person 12–15 to sexual penetration
notes: Nebraska age of consent is 16. Sexual assault of a child in the first degree carries 15 years to life. Second degree (§ 28-320.01) covers sexual contact with children under 16 (Class IIIA Felony for 12–15; Class IC Felony for under 12).

offense_class: Class III Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally disturbed the peace and quiet of any person, family, or neighborhood
By loud or unusual noise, tumultuous or offensive conduct, threatening, or fighting
notes: Nebraska uses 'disturbing the peace' rather than 'disorderly conduct.' Often used as a plea-down for more serious charges.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a peace officer
From effecting a lawful arrest
By using or threatening to use physical force or violence against the officer or another
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon during resistance
notes: Requires physical force or threat thereof. Passive resistance alone is not sufficient. Separate from obstructing a peace officer under § 28-906.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, impaired, or hindered
The enforcement of criminal law, preservation of the peace, or a government function
By using or threatening to use force, violence, or physical interference
notes: Broader than resisting arrest. Covers interference with any law enforcement or government function. Includes providing false information to officers.

offense_class: Varies (civil vs. criminal; direct vs. indirect)
penalty_max: 6 months (criminal contempt); indeterminate (civil contempt until compliance)
elements: Defendant engaged in disorderly conduct in the presence of the court
Or disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or willfully failed to comply with a court directive
notes: Direct contempt (in the courtroom) may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt (violation of court order outside courtroom) requires notice and hearing.

statute_title: Consumption of Alcohol in Public / Public Intoxication
offense_class: Class V Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant consumed alcoholic liquor on a public highway or in a public place
Or was publicly intoxicated to a degree that endangered self or others
notes: Minimal penalty — fine only, no jail. Many Nebraska municipalities have local ordinances with slightly different provisions.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (if felony charge); Class I Misdemeanor (if misdemeanor charge)
elements: Defendant was released on bail, bond, or own recognizance
Defendant was required to appear before a court at a specified time
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
notes: Penalty depends on the seriousness of the underlying charge. Court issues a bench warrant upon failure to appear. Bail is forfeited.

offense_class: Class II Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
About an alleged offense or incident
With the intent to mislead or obstruct
notes: Includes false reports of crimes and false emergency calls. Defendant may be liable for investigation costs.

offense_class: Class IV Felony
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any crime of violence
With intent to terrorize another person
Or to cause evacuation of a building, place of assembly, or public transportation
enhancements: Threat involving weapons of mass destruction
Threat targeting schools or public facilities
notes: Nebraska uses 'terroristic threats' for what other states call criminal threats. Includes bomb threats and threats against public facilities.

offense_class: Class II Felony (in a Class I or IA Felony proceeding); Class IV Felony (all other cases)
elements: Defendant made a materially false statement under oath or equivalent affirmation
In any official proceeding
The statement was material
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
enhancements: Perjury in a capital or Class IA Felony case (Class II Felony)
notes: Perjury in a capital or Class IA Felony proceeding is a Class II Felony — extremely severe. All other perjury is a Class IV Felony.

offense_class: Class IV Felony
elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer a benefit
Upon a public servant
As consideration for the public servant's decision, vote, or other official action
notes: Both offering and accepting bribes are criminal offenses. Public servant includes any government official or employee.

offense_class: Class IV Felony (from felony custody); Class I Misdemeanor (from misdemeanor custody)
penalty_max: 5 years (from felony custody); 1 year (from misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant was in official custody or detention
Defendant purposely effected escape from the place of detention
Or failed to return from authorized temporary absence
enhancements: Use of force or threat of force
Use of a weapon during escape
notes: Penalty graded by seriousness of the offense for which defendant was in custody. Sentence may be consecutive to original sentence.

offense_class: Class I Misdemeanor (first); Class IV Felony (second+; or if torture/serious injury/death)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly cruelly mistreated an animal
By beating, abandoning, or subjecting the animal to unnecessary suffering
Or by failing to provide proper food, water, or shelter
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class IV Felony)
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Repeated cruelty or aggravated acts become felonies. Animal fighting is separately criminalized.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose original sentence, continue probation with modified conditions, or impose graduated sanctions. Burden of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Board of Parole makes revocation decisions. May revoke parole and return offender to prison for the remainder of the sentence.

offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant, acting with the kind of culpability required for the offense
Aided, abetted, procured, or caused another person to commit the offense
Or conspired with another to commit the offense
notes: An accomplice is legally accountable for the conduct of the principal. Nebraska holds accomplices to the same liability as the person who directly committed the offense.

offense_class: One class lower than the completed offense (Class IA/IB attempted = Class II; Class II attempted = Class III; etc.)
penalty_max: Varies by class of attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of attempted offense
elements: Defendant, with intent to commit a specific crime
Engaged in conduct that constituted a substantial step
Toward the commission of the crime
notes: Attempt is graded one class below the completed offense. Attempt to commit a Class IA or IB Felony is a Class II Felony. Voluntary abandonment is an affirmative defense.

offense_class: One class lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in or cause the performance of conduct
Which constitutes a crime or an attempt to commit a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy
notes: Conspiracy is graded one class below the target offense. Requires at least one overt act. Renunciation is a defense if defendant thwarted the success of the conspiracy.
